## Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)

Everything you need to know about getting your pitch deck investor-ready

### How does the free pitch deck analysis work?

Upload your pitch deck (PDF or PowerPoint) and our AI analyzes it in under 60 seconds. You'll get scores across 10 categories including problem, solution, market size, traction, team, and more. The analysis is based on criteria used by real angel investors.

### Is the pitch deck analysis really free?

Yes, the AI pitch deck analysis is completely free with no credit card required. You can upload your deck and get instant feedback at no cost. We also offer additional services like mentorship and investor introductions for founders who want more support.

### What do investors look for in a pitch deck?

Angel investors evaluate pitch decks across 10 key areas: 1) Problem - is it real and painful? 2) Solution - does it solve the problem? 3) Market - is it big enough? 4) Traction - any early proof? 5) Business Model - how will you make money? 6) Competition - what's your moat? 7) Team - can you execute? 8) Go-to-Market - how will you acquire customers? 9) Ask - how much are you raising? 10) Vision - where is this going?

### How do I connect with angel investors?

After analyzing your pitch deck, our ML model matches you with relevant investors from our network of 1,200+ angels based on sector fit, stage preference, and investment thesis. Join our Discord community of 500+ members to access mentorship and warm introductions to investors.

### What stage startups do you work with?

We focus on pre-seed and seed stage startups. Whether you're building your first pitch deck or refining one for fundraising, our tools and community are designed to help early-stage founders get investor-ready.

### How many slides should a pitch deck have?

The optimal pitch deck length is 10-15 slides. This gives you enough space to cover the essential elements (problem, solution, market, traction, team, business model, competition, go-to-market, financials, and ask) without overwhelming investors. Many successful decks follow the classic 10-slide format popularized by Guy Kawasaki.
